skills.name: Code interpreter
skills.description: Let the model run Python in a sandboxed microVM and return stdout plus charts (matplotlib). Network is off; pandas/numpy/matplotlib are available. Requires a configured local sandbox.

skills.name: Image generation
skills.description: Let the model generate images via Minimax (text-to-image, or image-to-image when you provide a reference URL). Tight per-turn cap because each generation costs ~1–3¢.

skills.name: File search
skills.description: Let the model pull additional sections from your attached files when their inline view was truncated. Uses Postgres full-text search over each file's full extracted text. Sign-in required — file full text is stored in Supabase.

skills.name: Web fetch
skills.description: Let the model fetch a specific URL and read its contents. Pairs naturally with Web search — search finds the page, fetch reads it in full. Per-turn cap keeps it from going wild.

skills.name: Web search
skills.description: Look up current information on the web. Picks from Tavily and Brave under the hood — toggle providers and tune their settings in this skill's panel.

envVars.description: The default model: used when a request names none (/v1/summarize), for the follow-up-suggestion chips and for forced tool calls on a model without structured output. Must be a `config/models.json` id or the service refuses to boot. Empty → the default below.
AI Gateway (Vercel) — the catalog's `gateway` routes (OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek; `anthropic/*` too when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset).

Anthropic API key — `anthropic/*` models go to Anthropic directly with this key (each mapped to its `anthropicModelId`). Empty → those models go through the AI Gateway when it is configured, else a run on them fails with a message saying so (nothing falls back to canned output).
Optional Anthropic base-URL override for the direct Anthropic route. Empty → Anthropic's own API (https://api.anthropic.com, passed explicitly). Has no effect when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is empty.
(no description)

Code interpreter sandbox (optional). Set CODE_SANDBOX_ENABLED=1 to register the `runCode` skill and execute model-written Python/JS in a local microsandbox microVM (libkrun; HVF on Apple Silicon). Network is OFF inside the sandbox; pandas/numpy/matplotlib available (see image note below). Absent → the skill is simply not registered (no mock). CODE_SANDBOX_BASE_URL also enables it and is reserved for a future remote backend (the local microVM runtime ignores the URL). Needs `uv sync --extra sandbox` (services/agent-py/README.md § Code interpreter); see also docs/PLAN-execution-sandbox.md + docs/PLAN-code-interpreter.md.

Content-Security-Policy mode (optional). `proxy.ts` mints a per-request nonce and emits a strict nonce + 'strict-dynamic' policy (built by lib/server/security/csp.ts); violations are POSTed to agent-py's /v1/csp-report and logged there as `{"evt":"csp_violation",…}` lines. report-only (default) → Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only: nothing is blocked, violations are only reported enforce               → Content-Security-Policy: violations are blocked off                   → no CSP header at all (other security headers stay) Unset or unrecognised → report-only. Read docs/SECURITY.md before flipping to `enforce` (live-artifact / MCP-app frames inherit the policy).
(no description)

Embeddings — optional. Enables the vector / hybrid-retrieval pipeline (chunk + embed file text → pgvector, served by /v1/embed). Without it, retrieval stays full-text only. Points at an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings` endpoint; Ollama works (set EMBEDDINGS_BASE_URL to the same `/v1` URL, or leave blank to reuse OLLAMA_BASE_URL above). EMBEDDINGS_MODEL defaults to `nomic-embed-text` (768-dim — must match the vector(768) column in migration 0023).
(no description)
Cross-family verifier key — used when VERIFY_PROVIDER=google. Either GOOGLE_API_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY works (GOOGLE_API_KEY is checked first).

MCP private-host opt-in — optional, default off. Every MCP server URL (local-mode proxy calls, cloud-mode rows, saves) is SSRF-checked and must resolve to a public address. Set to `true` to also allow loopback / RFC 1918 / `.local`-style hosts — e.g. an MCP server on `http://localhost:3001/mcp` during single-user local dev. Link-local and cloud-metadata addresses (169.254.169.254 etc.) stay blocked even then. Do NOT enable on a shared/hosted deployment: any user could then point the server at your internal network. Only `true` enables it; a value other than `true` / `false` / empty stops agent-py at boot.

MCP encryption — required when any user picks Cloud-mode credentials for an MCP server. Generate with `openssl rand -base64 32`. The key lives only in agent-py's env, never in Postgres; it's passed as an argument to the SECURITY DEFINER encrypt/decrypt RPCs at request time. Rotating invalidates existing cloud-mode creds — users have to re-add the server. Leaving unset disables cloud mode (Local mode still works).

Memory-extraction model — optional. Distils durable facts from a finished chat turn when the user has memory on (/v1/memory/extract). Used when it is a `supportsStructuredOutput` model a provider serves; otherwise (or empty) AGENT_DEFAULT_MODEL.
(no description)

Minimax-CN — optional. When BOTH vars are set, the `minimax/*` models are served through Minimax's Anthropic-compatible endpoint. IMPORTANT: include the `/v1` suffix in the base URL. The Anthropic SDK appends `/messages` only — it doesn't add `/v1`. Example: MINIMAX_CN_BASE_URL=https://api.minimax.chat/anthropic/v1 The same key enables the `generateImage` tool (Minimax T2I / I2I via `/v1/image_generation`, derived from MINIMAX_CN_BASE_URL's origin; unset → `https://api.minimaxi.com`). Empty MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY → the tool is omitted.

Image generation rate limit. With MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY set, runs expose a `generateImage` tool (see Minimax-CN above). Each call costs ~1–3¢ depending on aspect ratio + count, so the per-IP limit defaults tight. Raise for trusted deployments behind auth; lower if you're seeing abuse. Not a positive number → 5, floored, capped at 60.

Path to config/models.json (the model allowlist; providers.json beside it). Empty → searched upward from the package (finds the repo root in a checkout); the Docker image sets /app/config/models.json.

Base URL of agent-py, the backend every surface talks to (chat on `/v1/runs`, tasks, schedules, files, MCP, the editor AI, …). Without it the app still builds, but shows a full-page "This deploy has no backend configured" screen pointing at the setup docs. Example: `http://localhost:8000` in dev — then also set CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3000 for agent-py (cross-origin). Same origin: set it to `/` when a reverse proxy serves agent-py on the frontend's own origin (PLAN-frontend-backend-split.md Q21) — requests go to `/v1/...` on the current origin and CSP needs no extra source. Local dev: `docker compose up proxy agent-py`, then open http://localhost:8080 (see README "Same-origin backend"). The CSP's report-uri / Reporting-Endpoints point at agent-py's `/v1/csp-report` (`/` → same-origin `/v1/csp-report`); unset → the policy has no report-uri.
Optional. An extra backend origin the browser may call, added to the CSP's `connect-src`. Leave empty unless you know you need it.
(no description)

Supabase — optional. When set, users can sign in (email + password) and sync workspaces, conversations, files, and conversation assets across devices. When unset, the app runs anonymously on localStorage only. These are the public URL and anon key; agent-py reads its own SUPABASE_URL / SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET / SUPABASE_DB_URL below.
(no description)

Ollama — optional. When OLLAMA_BASE_URL is set, the `ollama/*` models are served by that Ollama host (Ollama ≥ 0.14, its Anthropic-format endpoint), and it is the fallback embedder when EMBEDDINGS_BASE_URL is unset. Typical local value: `http://localhost:11434/v1`. OLLAMA_API_KEY is optional (Ollama doesn't enforce auth). The `ollama` provider is declared with `allowInsecureBaseUrl: true` in providers.json, which lets a loopback / `http://` URL through — only enable this for endpoints you fully control.
OpenRouter — optional. When set, the `openrouter/*` models are served against `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` (fixed in config/providers.json). Get a key from https://openrouter.ai/keys.

Require sign-in for AI — optional, default off. When `true` (or `1`) AND Supabase is configured, anonymous runs and the anonymous calls that spend model budget answer `401 { code: "auth_required" }`, and /v1/extract skips its vision pass for anonymous callers (plain text extraction still works). Off / unset / no Supabase → anonymous mode works as before. Accepted values: true, false, 1, 0 (case-insensitive). Anything else is a configuration error: anonymous calls fail with 500 until it's fixed (never silently open). The browser learns it from the 401, not from an env var.

Direct Postgres connection string. Required by the task worker, the scheduler, the reconciler and persisted runs, which need `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` semantics that the transaction pooler doesn't expose. Use the *direct* connection from Supabase's dashboard (the one ending in `db.<project>.supabase.co:5432`), NOT the pooler (`*.pooler.supabase.com:6543`). Empty in dev → the poller no-ops every tick (the service still serves /healthz + /readyz).
JWT secret — verifies HS256 access tokens. Find it under Project Settings → API → JWT Settings in the Supabase dashboard.

Service role key — agent-py's Supabase Storage access (with SUPABASE_URL): generated images and tool-made files are saved under `user-files/<user_id>/generated/...` (the model then gets a long-lived signed URL instead of a short-lived one). Without it generated images fall back to inline Minimax URLs (work for hours, then expire). Share pages read through SUPABASE_DB_URL instead.
Supabase project URL (the same value as NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL above). Reported by /readyz; the JWKS URL and Storage are derived from it.

Background-task safety net (agent-py's no-worker reconciler). agent-py executes every user's tasks unless an admin opts the user out (`auth.users.raw_app_meta_data->>'agent_backend'` set to anything but 'python'; their tasks fail up front). A task still `queued` and never started after this many minutes while NO worker executed anything in that window — agent-py's worker down or in WORKER_DRY_RUN — is failed with "No task worker available". A busy worker's backlog waits. Empty → 10.
Tavily — optional. Backs the `webSearch` tool. When unset the tool is omitted entirely, so the model never sees it.

Citation verifier model — optional. When set, a post-run citation pass runs on Deep Research reports: each cited claim is checked against its sources and the result shows a confidence chip + flagged claims (see docs/PLAN-citation-verifiability.md). Empty = OFF. Use a CHEAP model id (ideally cheaper/weaker than the answerer — cross-checking your own output is weaker). Uses the same ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL client, so it's a no-op without a key regardless.

Verifier provider family — optional. Default "anthropic" preserves the legacy same-family behaviour. Set to "google" to cross-check the answer with a different model family (a model is a weak judge of its own output). The Google path needs GOOGLE_API_KEY (or GEMINI_API_KEY) and the optional google-generativeai SDK; if either is missing it falls back to Anthropic with a one-shot log warning.

Vision document extraction (optional). Picks the vision-capable model /v1/extract uses to transcribe layout-rich / scanned PDFs (render pages → image → markdown tables/captions) on top of the text-only pass. Must name a model flagged `supportsVision` in config/models.json and served here. Unset → the first such model; if none, the vision pass is skipped (text-only extraction). See docs/PLAN-multimodal-docs.md. Example: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`.
Tests only. `true` runs background tasks on a model-free stub that answers canned text; empty / `false` is off, any other value fails the service at boot. Never set it in a deployment.
